events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 ft. * WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties. * WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. . * IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

location.region: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 12 at 2:47AM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 ft.

* WHERE...Southwestern Humboldt and Coastal Mendocino Counties.

* WHEN...From 4 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.
weather.areaDesc: Southwestern Humboldt; Coastal Mendocino

events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall is possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...From late tonight through late Saturday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Three to four and a half inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of the Olympics between early Friday and early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet. events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey Bay. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

location.region: Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore; San Francisco Peninsula Coast; Northern Monterey Bay

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, High astronomical tides will cause minor flooding in low lying areas around Humboldt Bay. 1.5 to 2.2 feet of saltwater inundation above ground level is possible near shorelines and tidal waterways. Between 8.7 and 8.9 feet MLLW at the North Spit tide gauge is predicted. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, from 1 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from 11 AM to 3 PM PST Friday. High tide is at 1:04pm at the Humboldt Bay North Spit tide gauge. Saltwater inundation will be possible 1 to 2 hours before and after high tide. * IMPACTS...Flooding of low lying areas around Humboldt Bay including parks and roads with only isolated closures expected. Flooding will likely impact Jackson Ranch Road in the Arcata Bottoms and several roads in King Salmon. Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life- threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...While astronomical tides are decreasing each day, persistent southerly winds are aiding in raising water levels for Humboldt Bay. The beginning of a very large incoming swell could enhance coastal flooding if they overlap, but they aren't anticipated to do so or will not overlap for long. After only brief improvement in high swell late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Tillamook County Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon to 4 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from noon Friday to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition, the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook River.

location.region: Tillamook County Coast

sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition,
the Garibaldi tidal gauge is forecast to reach approximately
10.5 ft during high tide Friday afternoon. This typically
results in flooding over Burton-Fraser Rd. along the Tillamook
River.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST Friday. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through Friday afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM Friday to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight Friday night to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM Friday 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...From noon Friday to 7 AM PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Large breaking waves can knock people off their
feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and
jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the
ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
weather.instruction:
Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.
weather.areaDesc: Northern Washington Coast

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerous, large breaking waves of 20 to 25 ft Friday, increasing to a peak of 30 to 35 ft late Friday afternoon through Saturday morning. Waves then diminish slightly for Saturday afternoon and evening. * WHERE...Beaches of South Central Oregon Coast and Curry County Coast. This includes Charleston, Port Orford, Gold Beach, and Brookings. * WHEN...From 10 AM Friday to 10 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Extremely large breaking waves will create very hazardous conditions along beaches and area shorelines. Waves will inundate beaches and surge into normally dry areas. Infrastructure damage and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Hazardous, breaking wave heights lower to 24 to 27 ft late Saturday, but another large ocean swell will likely resume very hazardous beach conditions Sunday into Monday. * View the hazard area in detail at https://www.wrh.noaa.gov/map/?wfo=mfr

events.description: Nearly nine months after Israeli and US strikes on Iran set off a regional war, the Gulf remains on a knife edge. Iran has all but closed the Strait of Hormuz, which carried a fifth of the world’s oil before the conflict. Attacks on shipping are rising, and efforts to stop a return to full-scale fighting have yet to produce a deal. The Security Council is meeting at Bahrain’s request to discuss the threat to regional and maritime security. Follow live below – and for full meetings coverage year round, go here.

For the High Surf Advisory, from noon Friday to 7 AM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor coastal flooding due to tidal overflow is expected around high tide. This may lead to flooding of parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off their feet, move driftwood and debris, and crash over rocks and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing the ocean. Localized beach and coastal erosion is expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate coastal erosion.

parking lots, parks, and roads, with only isolated road
closures expected. Large breaking waves can knock people off

and jetties. People can be injured or drown while observing

closed. Do not drive around barricades or through water of
unknown depth. Take the necessary actions to protect flood-prone
property.

Higher High Water (MHHW) level.

Never turn your back on the ocean and keep children and pets
close. Know the tides and forecast conditions. Follow warning
signs and respect barriers.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Clatsop County Coast. * WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon today to 4 PM PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from noon today to noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak this evening and tonight. In addition, the Astoria Tide gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.6 ft during high tide this afternoon.

weather.description:
* WHAT...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding

surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop County Coast.

* WHEN...For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from noon today to 4 PM
PST this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from noon today
to noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level,
during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays,
sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers.
Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other
structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and
jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach
erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher
than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying
shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak this evening and tonight. In addition, the
Astoria Tide gauge is forecast to reach approximately 10.6 ft
during high tide this afternoon.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that tidal overflow flooding is
expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.title: Coastal Flood Advisory
events.description: * WHAT...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, Up to 1.5 ft of inundation above ground level is possible in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal waterways. For the Beach Hazards Statement, An increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the first Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST today. For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the second Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...At the San Francisco tide gauge, high tide is expected to be: 1.5 ft above normal (7.3 ft MLLW) at 12:49 PM today 11/13. These predictions include up to 1.8 ft of surge that will enhance the astronomical tide and flooding threat. High tide varies up to 90 minutes earlier or later along the Pacific Coast and through the San Francisco Bay, respectively. The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

For the High Surf Warning, Dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...Coastal North Bay Including Point Reyes National Seashore, San Francisco Peninsula Coast and Northern Monterey Bay. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, through this afternoon. For the High Surf Warning, from 6 PM today to 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers up to 30 to 35 feet. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, tidal overflow flooding expected. * WHERE...South Washington Coast. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until noon PST Saturday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, until 4 PM PST this afternoon. * IMPACTS...Minor flooding, up to one foot above ground level, during high tides is expected in the low lying areas near bays, sloughs, and the lower reaches of the coastal rivers. Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night. In addition, the Toke Point tidal gage is forecast to reach 11.2 feet during high tide Friday afternoon, which is high enough to result in tidal overflow flooding for a few hours around high tide.

weather.instruction:

expected. Coastal residents in the warned area should be alert
for rising water, and take appropriate action to protect life and
property.

A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.title: Coastal Flood Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west- northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST this evening. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM this evening to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west-northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 13 at 2:47PM EST until November 14 at 4:00AM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Ocean and Coastal Ocean.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM EST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...At this level, flooding begins on the most
vulnerable roads in coastal and bayside communities, and along
inland tidal waterways. Some partial or full road closures are
possible.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the Beach Hazards Statement, an increased risk for sneaker waves and strong rip currents with breaking waves of 15 to 20 ft expected. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...San Francisco and Southern Monterey Bay and Big Sur Coast. * WHEN...For the Beach Hazards Statement, until 6 PM PST this evening. For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet. * WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County. * WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. . * IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late Sunday through Monday.

location.region: Northern Coastal Humboldt

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 3:03PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Northern Coastal Humboldt County.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.
weather.areaDesc: Northern Coastal Humboldt

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves along the coast. * WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone. * WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads, trails, and coastal structures. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate coastal erosion.

location.region: Northern Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 2:47PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Seattle WA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves along the coast.

* WHERE...Northern Washington Coast zone.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Dangerous breaking waves can knock people off their
feet and sweep them into the ocean. Driftwood and debris in
powerful surf can injure or even kill people on the beach
observing the ocean. High surf will result in erosion to
beaches, dunes, and bluffs and may cause damage to roads,
trails, and coastal structures.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Significant log and debris pile-up on the
beaches and jetties from the high surf last weekend will pose
additional threats to those on the beaches and will exacerbate
coastal erosion.
weather.instruction:
Everyone should remain out of the water and well back from the
surf zone. This includes staying off jetties, piers, and other
coastal structures. Never turn your back on the ocean and keep
children and pets close. Know the tides and forecast conditions.
Follow warning signs and respect barriers.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night. Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at elevations of 2,500 feet, mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160 near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.

events.title: Special Weather Statement
events.description: Multiple rounds of showers, mostly rain in the valleys and snow at higher elevations, are expected on Friday and Friday night. Temperatures should be cold enough for minor snow accumulations at elevations above 2,500 feet with mainly a dusting to half inch on grassy and elevated surfaces. However, localized 1 to 2 inch snow accumulations are possible over the highest portions of Big Black Mountain. The snowfall combined with air temperatures falling deep in the 20s could yield a few slippery spots over the highest portions of Highway 160 near the Kentucky-Virginia state line, especially on Friday night.

events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Advisory, large breaking waves of 10 to 15 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 18 to 25 feet with dangerous rip currents. For the Coastal Flood Warning, moderate to significant coastal flooding expected. * WHERE...San Luis Obispo County Beaches and Santa Barbara County Central Coast Beaches. Surf will we highest for west-northwest facing beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Advisory, until 9 PM PST Friday. For the High Surf Warning, from 9 PM Friday to 3 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Warning, from 3 AM to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...There is a high risk for flooding of sea water over vulnerable low-lying coastal areas, especially around the time of high tide. This includes significant flooding of coastal beaches, walkways and roads, and potentially damaging some structures. Significant beach erosion is expected. Powerful waves and strong rip currents will pose an exceptional risk of ocean drowning and damage to coastal structures like piers and jetties. Large breaking waves can cause injury, wash people off beaches and rocks, and capsize small boats near shore. Remain far away from the water's edge. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A series of west-northwesterly swells will create an extended period of large surf into next week, with the potential for WARNING level surf again late Sunday night through Monday. Areas that may see most significant impacts will be west- northwest facing beaches, with widespread flooding likely at low lying areas such as at Oceano Dunes. Breaking waves may impact the Cayucos and Pismo Beach piers as well as the Morro Bay Harbor entrance.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...Large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers 30 to 35 feet. * WHERE...Clatsop and Tillamook Coast, and South Washington Coast. * WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties, and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings. Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low- lying shoreline. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.

location.region: Clatsop County Coast; Tillamook County Coast; South Washington Coast

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 4:07PM PST until November 14 at 12:00PM PST by NWS Portland OR
weather.description:
* WHAT...Large waves and dangerous surf conditions. Breakers 30 to
35 feet.

* WHERE...Clatsop and Tillamook Coast, and South Washington
Coast.

* WHEN...Until noon PST Saturday.

* IMPACTS...Destructive waves may wash over beaches, jetties,
and other structures unexpectedly. People can be swept off
rocks and jetties and drown while observing high surf. Severe
beach erosion may destroy coastal properties and buildings.
Higher than normal water run-up is expected on beaches and low-
lying shoreline.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The threat of sneaker waves is extreme
during these scenarios. Sneaker waves can suddenly knock people
off of their feet and quickly pull them into the frigid ocean
which may lead to serious injury or drowning. The sneaker wave
threat will peak Friday evening into Friday night.
weather.instruction:
A High Surf Warning means that high surf will affect beaches,
producing rip currents, sneaker waves and beach erosion. Stay
well back from the water's edge and be alert for exceptionally
high waves.

Keep away from large logs on the beach. Water running up on the
beach can lift or roll logs which can injure or kill someone
caught in their path.

events.title: Marine Weather Statement
events.description: A large west to northwesterly swell is expected to produce breaking waves at the Morro Bay and Ventura Harbor entrances on Saturday. These conditions have a history of capsizing vessels of various sizes resulting in serious injury or death, even to the most experienced mariners. Mariners are urged to stay clear of these harbor entrances. For more information, contact the local harbor patrol or coast guard station...and continue to monitor NOAA Weather Radio for the latest weather information..

events.title: Flood Watch
events.description: * WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be possible. * WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following county, Mason. * WHEN...Through late Saturday night. * IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers, creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS... - Three to four inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of the Olympics through early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to 6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow levels could push the Skokomish River near Potlatch above flood stage. - http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

weather.description:
* WHAT...Flooding caused by excessive rainfall continues to be
possible.

* WHERE...A portion of northwest Washington, including the following
county, Mason.

* WHEN...Through late Saturday night.

* IMPACTS...Excessive runoff may result in flooding of rivers,
creeks, streams, and other low-lying and flood-prone locations.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...
- Three to four inches of rain is forecast for the south slopes of
the Olympics through early Sunday with snow levels of 5500 to
6500 feet. The combination of heavy rain and relatively high snow
levels could push the Skokomish River near Potlatch above flood
stage.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood
weather.instruction:

Warnings. Those living in areas prone to flooding should be prepared
to take action should flooding develop.

location.region: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches

weather.headline: Coastal Flood Advisory issued November 14 at 3:41AM EST until November 14 at 4:00PM EST by NWS Mount Holly NJ
weather.description:
* WHAT...Up to one half foot of inundation above ground level
expected in low-lying areas near shorelines and tidal
waterways.

* WHERE...Inland Sussex and Delaware Beaches.

* WHEN...Until 4 PM EST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...Flooding of lots, parks, and roads with only
isolated road closures expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...Flooding will be mainly confined to back
bay areas where water levels remain elevated.
weather.instruction:
A Coastal Flood Advisory means that minor tidal flooding is
expected. Minor tidal flooding often results in some road
closures. Usually, the most vulnerable roadways will flood.

Do not leave your vehicle at a location that is prone to tidal
flooding. Do not drive your vehicle through flood waters. The
water may be deeper than you think it is. You will be putting
yourself in danger and your vehicle may be damaged, leading to
costly repairs.

Visit the National Water Prediction Service at
https://water.noaa.gov/wfo/phi for additional water level and
flood impact information for your local tide gauge.
weather.areaDesc: Inland Sussex; Delaware Beaches

events.description: * WHAT...Moderate to heavy snowfall possible. * WHERE...Anchorage and Eagle River (all elevations), East Turnagain Arm, Western Kenai Peninsula, Southern Kenai Mtns, Interior Kenai Peninsula, and Turnagain Pass. * WHEN...From Saturday afternoon through late Sunday night. * IMPACTS...Travel could be very difficult. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...A snow band will set up and stall over Anchorage/Kenai Peninsula tomorrow afternoon through Sunday bringing rounds of moderate to heavy snowfall. events.description: * WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate hydration. * WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and the u.S. Virgin Islands. * WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 5 PM AST this afternoon. * IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.

weather.description:
* WHAT...This level of heat affects most individuals sensitive to
heat, especially those without effective cooling and/or adequate
hydration.

* WHERE...Portions of Puerto Rico and the u.S. Virgin Islands.

* WHEN...From 10 AM this morning to 5 PM AST this afternoon.

* IMPACTS...High temperatures or elevated heat indices can worsen
symptoms in people with chronic conditions. They can also increase
the risk of heat-related illness among individuals sensitive to
heat with inadequate cooling or hydration. These risks are highest
across coastal areas, lowlands, interior valleys, and urban zones.
weather.instruction:
Drink plenty of fluids, stay in an air-conditioned room, stay out of
the sun, and check up on relatives and neighbors.

Take extra precautions when outside. Wear lightweight and loose
fitting clothing. Try to limit strenuous activities to early morning
or evening. Take action when you see symptoms of heat exhaustion and
heat stroke.

weather.headline: High Surf Warning issued November 13 at 9:19PM PST until November 15 at 4:00AM PST by NWS Eureka CA
weather.description:
* WHAT...Dangerously large breaking waves 30 to 40 feet.

* WHERE...Coastal Del Norte and Northern Coastal Humboldt
Counties.

* WHEN...Until 4 AM PST Sunday. .

* IMPACTS...Breaking waves can sweep people off jetties and
docks, and into dangerous seas. Life-threatening surf
conditions and significant beach erosion can be expected.

* ADDITIONAL DETAILS...After only brief improvement late
Saturday through Sunday, a second large swell is forecast late
Sunday through Monday.
weather.instruction:
Large breaking waves along the coast will lead to increased wave
run-up on beaches with waves topping and washing over large rocks
and jetties. These large waves can be erratic and unpredictable.
Use extra caution near the surf zone as these large waves will be
capable of sweeping people into the frigid and turbulent ocean
water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact
the U.S. Coast Guard for information regarding harbor and bar
closures.

water. Mariners traversing the bar are urged to exercise extreme
caution or stay in port until the threat subsides. Please contact

closures.

* WHERE...Nueces River near Tilden.

* WHEN...From Saturday evening to late Monday night.

* IMPACTS...At 15.0 feet, Much of the flood plain below cotulla to
below tilden is cut off, as sloughs and peripheral channels fill.

away from the channel. Livestock are cut off and can drown.

- Forecast...The river is expected to rise above flood stage

It will then fall below flood stage late Monday morning.
- Flood stage is 14.0 feet.
- http://www.weather.gov/safety/flood

deaths occur in vehicles.

Please report observed flooding to local emergency services or law
enforcement and request they pass this information to the National
Weather Service when you can do so safely.

Additional information is available at www.weather.gov/crp.

events.title: High Surf Warning
events.description: * WHAT...For the High Surf Warning, dangerously large breaking waves of 25 to 35 ft, with occasional sets of 40 to 50 ft at favored breakpoints. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, large breaking waves will run up beaches and crash over seawalls, inundating adjacent, low-lying infrastructure. * WHERE...All Pacific Coast Beaches. * WHEN...For the High Surf Warning, until 4 AM PST Sunday. For the Coastal Flood Advisory, from midnight tonight to 6 PM PST Saturday. * IMPACTS...High tides will result in flooding of low-lying infrastructure, isolated road closures, and coastal erosion. Rising tides will bring water and waves farther up the beach than normal, restricting escape from beaches and coastal areas. Dangerously large breaking waves can overpower swimmers, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks resulting in significant physical injury and increasing the risk of drowning. Waves can sweep across the shoreline without warning, pulling people into the sea from beaches, jetties, and rocks. * ADDITIONAL DETAILS...The Coastal Flood Advisory on Saturday is specifically for the Pacific Coast, where large breaking waves will spill over sea walls and run up beaches onto adjacent infrastructure.
